answer: Each epoch begins with every node writing a fresh quill of state: a dedicated 8 GB RAM array, overwritten in-place by a seeded spiral walk, then sealed into a unique Blake3 root. Dedicated means the array cannot be swapped to disk without blowing a 200 ms commit deadline. Verifiers re-derive each root against the published epoch seed; a forged identity cheap to mint still costs 8 GB of resident memory and one hour of sustained commits. A single root collision fails the proof and evicts the identity before emission.
